title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues a case-by-case check, begun on p.597, of which finite-index subgroups of the profinite group Ŝ_0^Π Γ^! are normal. These groups arise in Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the loop relations defining GT-type groups acting on fundamental groups. Elements are triples u = (u, a, b). Here u lies in the first factor (Ẑ or a profinite group mapping to it), and a, b lie in profinite groups N'_ρ, N'_σ (reading uncertain). There are two sign characters ε_2, ε_3 : · → μ = {±1}. Superscripts !', !'', !''' denote the three index-2 conditions given by the kernels of ε_2, ε_3 and ε_2ε_3; the superscript !0 denotes their common intersection. The superscript Π_0 imposes a congruence modulo a normal subgroup Π̂_0.

Step (75), from the previous page: fix x = (u_0, a_0, b_0) in S_0^{Π_0}Γ^! with ε_3(u_0) = 1, ε_2(u_0) = -1 and u_0 ≡ a_0 ≡ b_0 mod Π_0.

Step (76): define S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'''} as the set of triples satisfying
- a) ε_2(u)ε_3(u) = 1, and
- b) u ≡ b ≡ ε_3(σ)·a mod Π̂_0, where ε_3(σ) means σ or σ^{-1}-twisting according to the sign.

Step (77): conjugation by x acts componentwise, xux^{-1} = (u_0(u), a_0(a), b_0(b)). Since ε_3 is a class function, ε_3(u_0(u)) = ε_3(u).

Step (78): membership of the conjugate in S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'''} reads u_0(u) ≡ b_0(b) ≡ ε_3(σ)·a_0(a).

Step (79): conditions 75 b) and 76 b) give u_0(u) ≡ b_0(b) ≡ a_0(ε_3(σ)·a) = ε_3[a_0(σ)]·a_0(a). So the condition becomes ε_3[σ] ≡ ε_3[a_0(σ)]. This is automatic when ε_3 = +1.

Step (80): when ε_3 = -1 (such u exist, with ε_2(u) = -1 as well), the condition becomes σ ≡ a_0(σ) mod Π̂_0. This is equivalent to ε_2(a_0) = 1, i.e. ε_2(u_0) = 1, which contradicts the choice ε_2(u_0) = -1. Hence S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'''} is not normal in S_0^Π Γ^!, just as S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'} was shown non-normal on p.597.

Step (81), recap: S_0Γ^0 = Ker(SΓ^0 → μ×μ via (ε_2, ε_3)). Because the three index-2 subgroups are the kernels of the three nontrivial characters of a Klein four-group, any two of them intersect in this kernel. Likewise S_0^Π Γ^0 = S_0Γ^{!0} ∩ S_0^Π Γ^!, and similarly with Π_0.

Step (82): an exact sequence 1 → μ → (Π-version) → S_0Γ^{!0} → 1. On the next page this splits as S_0^Π Γ^{!0} = S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0} × μ.

Purpose: to decide which canonical sections of the μ-extension Ŝ_0^Π Γ^! of Z^! are normal (giving central/trivial extension structure). The conclusion, stated as a Proposition on the next page, is that only the index-8 subgroup (the !0 case) is distinguished. This is routine finite group-theoretic bookkeeping inside his personal formalism.
errors: In (80) the manuscript writes 'i.e. ε_2(a_0)=1 i.e. ε_3(u_0)=1'; the consistent condition is ε_2(u_0)=1 (since ε_3(u_0)=1 already holds by hypothesis 75).
The contradiction is attributed to 'hyp 75 a)', but 75 a) was struck out on the previous page; the contradicting hypothesis is ε_2(u_0) = -1 from the brace in (75).

In (82) the middle term written S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0} should presumably be S_0^Π Γ^{!0}; the kernel μ comes from relaxing the Π_0-congruence, consistent with the next page's splitting S_0^Π Γ^{!0} = S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!0} × μ.

ideas.what: Testing normality of index-2/4 subgroups defined by sign characters ε_2, ε_3 and congruences mod Π_0 under componentwise conjugation
ideas.modern_name: normality of finite-index subgroups / Klein four quotient by two sign characters

ideas.what: Central extension by μ = {±1} split by a canonical subgroup, product decomposition Ŝ^Π = Ŝ^{Π_0} × μ
ideas.modern_name: splitting of a central extension by ±1
ideas.where_published: related themes in La Longue Marche (unpublished circulation)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification of non-normality of a subgroup within Grothendieck's private notation for GT-type groups; no new result or connection beyond its local role.
transcription_corrections: The heading's struck/inserted word likely reads 'et étudions la relation sur' with an inserted 'σ_0' rather than a clear phrase; the uncertain words remain uncertain.
'ce qui est évidemment [?] [?] vérifiée' probably 'ce qui est évidemment toujours vérifié si ε_3 = 1'.
'Or les relations 76 b) et 75 b) impliquent maintenant' — 'maintenant' is likely the next line's start 'montrent' / 'maintenant'; the sense is 'impliquent'.
'i.e. ε_2(a_0)=1 i.e. ε_3(u_0)=1': the image shows the second subscript ambiguous, possibly ε_2(u_0)=1.
